title: Speed up Git fixture construction behind the builder

# Dough Intent Coverage: SEED-262#reuse-immutable-git-histories

**Outcome: Caught.**

## Story and revision

- Story: SEED-262#reuse-immutable-git-histories (seed `.planning/seeds/SEED-262-faster-dashboard-test-feedback.md`, anchor `reuse-immutable-git-histories`).
- Revision checked: 8033e4119aa37e6fa56a601dae699128580c2a4e (product change 08d208fd0) on branch `claude/speed-up-git-fixture-construction-behind-the-bui`, in a detached scratch worktree at `/Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/d6536f37/tmp/intent-scratch` (pre-probe state: HEAD 8033e4119, `git status --porcelain` empty; dependencies installed with `node scripts/setup-native.mjs npm`, "npm acquisition complete").

## Promise

Key example 2, last sentence, backed by the Architecture note: "Removing the shared source after materialization leaves both returned copies usable" because "the Git copy has to remain usable after the shared base disappears, so Git alternates and writable hardlinks are unsuitable." Expected observable behavior: after the run's snapshot directory is deleted, each materialized copy's origin and integration checkout pass `git fsck --full`, resolve `HEAD^{commit}`, and can commit and push again.

## Fault

`tests/support/repository-template.mjs`, `startTemplate`: the integration checkout borrowed the snapshot's object store through Git alternates instead of copying it. The `cpSync(source.integration, integration, { recursive: true })` call was replaced by a `cpSync` with a filter that skips `source.integration/.git/objects`, followed by writing `<integration>/.git/objects/info/alternates` naming the snapshot's `integration/.git/objects` (plus `mkdirSync`/`writeFileSync` imports). Fixture and assertions were untouched. The template is later copied to callers by `materializeRepository` (`tests/support/repository-fixture.mjs`), so the alternates file travels into every returned copy.

## Fixture and maintained assertion

- Test: `tests/support/repository-snapshot-isolation.test.mjs`, "a copy of the shared history keeps its own refs, config, index and files when its peer writes or is removed, and outlives the snapshot".
- Fixture: `snapshotPreparedByRun(t, sharedHistory().please())` (queued, taken) offered through `offerSharedHistory`; two copies (`first`, `second`) and a `later` copy materialized from `completedBy("peer", 5)`.
- Intended assertion: after `rmSync(snapshot, ...)`, `await git(copy.integration, "fsck", "--full")` for `second` and `later`, then `cat-file -t HEAD^{commit}` and a commit/push on `later`.
- Focused command (scratch root, Homebrew bash first on PATH): `npm test -- tests/support/repository-snapshot-isolation.test.mjs`, with `OPEN_DOUGH_TEST_OUTCOMES`/`OPEN_DOUGH_TEST_TIMES` files recording the verdict because the runner is quiet on pass.

## Run observations

1. Baseline (unmodified): runner outcome `passed`, 1.0 s; `node --test --test-reporter=tap` on the same file confirmed the single test ran: `ok 1 - a copy of the shared history keeps its own refs...`, `# pass 1`.
2. Fault applied (`git diff --stat`: 1 file, 12 insertions, 2 deletions): runner outcome `failed`, exit 1. The test failed at `git fsck --full` on the copy's integration checkout after the snapshot removal: `error: unable to normalize alternate object path: /var/folders/.../repository-snapshot-ro8R5T/integration/.git/objects`, `missing commit 21687acd...`, `missing tree ed94b24b...`, `broken link from commit 0d4e6001... to commit 21687acd...`, exit code 10. The copy's origin `fsck` immediately before it passed, so the run reached the intended assertion on the intended copy.
3. Reach and wrong-behavior evidence, independent of the test: a throwaway script (`/Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/d6536f37/tmp/observe.mjs`, outside the checkout) prepared a snapshot, registered the prefix, materialized one copy and observed `copy alternates present: true` pointing at the snapshot's `integration/.git/objects`; after removing the snapshot the copy's `fsck --full` failed with the same unnormalizable-alternate and missing-object errors (only the locally committed completion still resolved via `cat-file`). The returned copy was no longer usable without the shared source, which is exactly the promised behavior gone wrong.
4. Restoration: the original file was copied back; `git status --porcelain` empty; `cmp` against `git show 8033e4119:tests/support/repository-template.mjs` identical. Rerun: runner outcome `passed`, 1.0 s. Scratch worktree then removed with `git worktree remove --force` and pruned; the execution checkout's six planning-file changes belong to the concurrent wrap-up, not to this probe, and no file under the execution checkout was edited here.

Earlier discarded attempts (same promise), reported for completeness: (a) hardlinking the origin with `cp -Rl` at `startTemplate` left the test green, but with no wrong behavior on the returned copies, because `materializeRepository` re-copies the template with `cpSync`, so the hardlinks never reach callers; this is not an assertion gap. (b) `git clone --shared` for the integration checkout failed the test earlier, at the peer's `git commit` ("Author identity unknown"), because the clone also dropped the checkout's identity config; that masks the alternates path, so it was replaced by the filtered-copy-plus-alternates fault above. Both edits were reverted and the tree verified clean before the next attempt.

## Cost

- **Test runtime:** measured. Runner-reported job time for the focused file: baseline 1.0 s, faulted run 0.8 s, restored run 1.0 s (`OPEN_DOUGH_TEST_TIMES`); `npm test` wall clock per run about 1.2 s (`Date.now()` around the command). Earlier discarded faulted runs 1.0 s and 0.6 s.
- **Human effort:** unavailable. No human action occurred between invocation and this report; no separately supported measure exists.
- **Agent effort:** estimated. About 17 tool calls (reads, scratch worktree creation, dependency install at about 2 s, 6 focused test runs, one observation script, restoration, cleanup); no token or wall-clock accounting of the agent's own reasoning is available separately from the elapsed entry below.
- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 419817 ms (measured), from 1794157577804 to 1794157997621 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.
